parties.defendant: Arlette Joelle Marie Madeleine Yao Affi

rule_source.governing_principle: Cooke J. §2: 'Where costs are ordered on the indemnity basis, there is no room for arguments of proportionality – only of reasonableness of the costs incurred.'

objections.label: claimant_did_work_himself
objections.summary: Defendant: costs claimed in respect of Hadef & Partners' bill must include work the Claimant did personally, and so are not reasonable.

objections.label: double_counsel_charged_for_hearing
objections.summary: Defendant: costs of two lawyers were claimed for the hearing when only one attended.
objections.evidence_note: Both lawyers attended the hearing online (Cooke J. §3).

objections.label: excess_senior_associate_time
objections.summary: Court's own residual observation on examining the Schedule of Costs: 'some excess in the overall time spent by the senior associate'.

human_ruling.operative_paragraph: IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT the Defendant shall pay the Claimant the sum of AED 120,000 within 14 days of the date of this order.
human_ruling.constructive_finding: Indemnity-basis review on these facts is the canonical bounded-discretion case: the rule (reasonableness only, no proportionality) cannot derive a single award figure. The protocol mechanically disposes of objection 1 (no named line item — Cooke J. §4 'without any specific complaint about any element of them'), holds objection 2 deterministically at zero on the evidence, and surfaces objection 3 — the Court's own residual qualitative concern — as the irreducible human-judgment region. The AED 8,914.80 reduction (~6.92% of claim) is the structured-discretion residue. The protocol bounds, but does not eliminate, that residue.
human_ruling.comparator_note: Across the three traces — Trace #1 (pure formula, AED 7,121.75 derived), Trace #2 (deferred conditional, retroactive interest from order date), Trace #3 (bounded discretion, AED 8,914.80 residue) — the protocol covers static rules, conditional rules, and rule-bounded human judgment. Trace #3 is the honest case for what the protocol cannot do, and is therefore the methodologically necessary third example.
